newsitem.title: USA: U.S. criticizes Franco-Cuban investment pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S. criticizes Franco-Cuban investment pact.

text.p: The United States on Thursday voiced muted criticism of a forthcoming economic agreement between France and Cuba and said it hoped Paris would continue to fight for human rights on the communist-ruled island.
France and Cuba are to sign an investment protection and promotion accord Friday in Paris. Cuba has similar bilateral agreements with nearly 20 countries.

Noting that the United States had imposed an economic boycott on Cuba for more than 30 years, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said: "We do not favour any other countries normalising their economic relations with Cuba."
"But what we prefer to do...and particularly with the European union members, is turn our joint attention on the human rights situation in Cuba," Burns told a news briefing.
"We hope that the French government -- while it's taking the step economically -- will also remain active in the fight for human rights in Cuba," he added.

The cautious U.S. tone appeared to reflect the defusing of tensions between Washington and the EU since Brussels asked the World Trade Organisation (WTO) Monday to suspend a panel looking into a row between the two trade powers over Cuba.

The move followed a deal whereby the EU agreed to hold off on its WTO action in return for a U.S. pledge to work for a softening of the Helms-Burton law, which seeks to punish some non-U.S. firms dealing with Cuba.
